title: Prototype: redesign the download-site screen into a striking liquid-glass landing page
story: The download page in the design prototype now looks like a real product landing page, not a plain list. The big green button for my own computer comes first, a little picture of the app shows what Grillo looks like, and the steps read as a clear numbered flow. If my computer asks for less motion, the soft glowing background stays still.

checks.criterion: The redesigned screen shows every part of the landing page, in both states
checks.steps: Open docs/ux/prototypes/grillo/index.html from disk, click '9 Download site', then click 'Pilot release, unsigned'. Then click 'Signed release'.
checks.expected: Pilot: logo and large 'Grillo', one-line pitch, filled 'Download for Windows' first with 'Download for Mac' beside it, release line with 'All releases on GitHub', a glass app-window mock, three feature cards, a five-step numbered flow with icons, 'What you need first', the amber warning note and the Windows and Mac install steps. Signed: same page with 'Download for Mac' first and a 'signed' badge, no warning note, two install steps per system.

checks.criterion: With reduced motion asked for, nothing moves
checks.steps: Turn on the system's reduce-motion setting (Windows: Settings, Accessibility, Visual effects, Animation effects off), then open the screen.
checks.expected: The coloured glow behind the panels stands still; with the setting off it drifts slowly.

checks.criterion: The screen is readable at phone width
checks.steps: Open the screen at 390 px wide (browser developer tools, phone size).
checks.expected: A single column, full-width download buttons and a vertical step timeline; nothing cut off, no sideways scrolling.
